source: ClawGuard Initial Database (based on BUILD_SPEC patterns)

indicators.description: Socket connection - potential reverse shell or C2 communication
indicators.false_positive_notes: Legitimate network clients may use this. Check destination.

indicators.description: Subprocess spawning a shell - high likelihood of reverse shell
indicators.false_positive_notes: Very rare legitimate use. Almost always malicious.

indicators.description: System call with netcat or interactive bash
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate use case. Always malicious.

indicators.description: PTY spawn - creates pseudo-terminal, often used in reverse shells
indicators.false_positive_notes: Rare legitimate use in terminal emulation. Flag for review.

indicators.description: HTTP request containing sensitive data (env vars, SSH keys, AWS creds)
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if destination is expected API endpoint.

indicators.description: URL request with sensitive data exfiltration
indicators.false_positive_notes: Verify the URL destination is legitimate.

indicators.description: Reading sensitive system files (passwords, SSH keys, AWS credentials)
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate skill should access these files.

indicators.description: Executing base64-decoded content - classic obfuscation technique
indicators.false_positive_notes: Almost always malicious. No legitimate use.

indicators.description: Evaluating base64-decoded content - obfuscated code execution
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate use. Always malicious.

indicators.description: Crontab manipulation - may establish persistence
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if skill legitimately needs scheduling.

indicators.description: Systemd service manipulation - may establish persistence
indicators.false_positive_notes: Skills should not manage system services.

indicators.description: Init.d script manipulation - legacy persistence mechanism
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate skill use case.

indicators.description: Shell profile modification - persistence through login shells
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if modification is legitimate (e.g., PATH updates).

indicators.description: Cryptocurrency mining software references
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate skill use case.

indicators.description: Mining-related terminology in code
indicators.false_positive_notes: May appear in blockchain-related legitimate skills.

indicators.description: RSA private key marker - credential exfiltration
indicators.example: if 'BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY' in content: send(content)
indicators.false_positive_notes: Skills should never handle private keys.

indicators.description: OpenSSH private key marker - credential exfiltration
indicators.false_positive_notes: Skills should never handle SSH keys.

indicators.description: AWS Access Key ID prefix - potential credential handling
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate if skill is AWS-related. Verify usage.

indicators.description: OpenAI API key pattern - potential credential exposure
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate in AI skills. Check if key is hardcoded.

indicators.description: GitHub Personal Access Token prefix
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate in GitHub skills. Check if hardcoded.

indicators.description: Bash /dev/tcp reverse shell technique
indicators.false_positive_notes: No legitimate use. Always malicious.

indicators.description: Raw socket creation - may be used for network attacks
indicators.false_positive_notes: Legitimate in networking skills. Review context.

indicators.description: HTTP request - check for data exfiltration
indicators.false_positive_notes: Very common in legitimate skills. Check destination URL.

indicators.description: HTTP server creation - may expose local services
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate for local development skills.

indicators.description: Opening files outside skill directory
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if access is to expected system files.

indicators.description: Directory traversal outside skill directory
indicators.example: for root, dirs, files in os.walk('/home'):
indicators.false_positive_notes: Skills should not scan system directories.

indicators.description: File manipulation - may delete or move critical files
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check source and destination paths carefully.

indicators.description: Dynamic code execution - may execute malicious code
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check what is being executed. Avoid user input.

indicators.description: Dynamic evaluation - may execute malicious expressions
indicators.false_positive_notes: Extremely dangerous with user input. Review carefully.

indicators.description: Dynamic import - may load malicious modules
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate for plugin systems. Review context.

indicators.description: Subprocess execution - may run malicious commands
indicators.false_positive_notes: Common in skills. Verify commands are safe.

indicators.description: System command execution
indicators.false_positive_notes: subprocess is preferred. Check command carefully.

indicators.description: Base64 decoding - may hide malicious payload
indicators.false_positive_notes: Common for data handling. Check what is decoded.

indicators.description: ROT13 decoding - simple obfuscation technique
indicators.false_positive_notes: Often used to hide malicious imports.

indicators.description: Marshal deserialization - can execute arbitrary code
indicators.false_positive_notes: Very rare legitimate use. Usually malicious.

indicators.description: Pickle deserialization - arbitrary code execution vulnerability
indicators.false_positive_notes: Never use with untrusted data. Review carefully.

indicators.description: Direct environment variable access
indicators.false_positive_notes: Common and often legitimate. Check what is accessed.

indicators.description: Environment variable retrieval
indicators.false_positive_notes: Common in skills. Verify necessity.

indicators.description: Clipboard access - may steal clipboard content
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate for clipboard utilities.

indicators.description: Input monitoring library - potential keylogger
indicators.false_positive_notes: Rare legitimate use. Usually malicious.

indicators.description: Keyboard capture - potential keylogger
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate for hotkey skills. Review carefully.

indicators.description: Screenshot capture - may capture sensitive information
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate for automation skills.

indicators.description: Runtime package installation - may install malicious packages
indicators.false_positive_notes: Skills should declare dependencies, not install at runtime.

indicators.description: File permission modification
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate. Check what permissions are set.

indicators.description: File deletion
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check what files are being deleted.

indicators.description: Daemon thread - may run in background persistently
indicators.false_positive_notes: Check if background processing is legitimate.

indicators.description: ctypes import - allows calling C functions directly
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate for system integration.

indicators.description: DNS lookup - may be reconnaissance
indicators.false_positive_notes: May be legitimate networking. Check purpose.

indicators.description: URL shortener - may hide malicious destination
indicators.false_positive_notes: Skills should use full URLs. Flag for review.

indicators.description: Suspicious TLD - commonly used for malicious domains
indicators.false_positive_notes: Some legitimate sites use these TLDs. Verify domain.
